Proposal to take over Nilachal Ispat .Nigam Ltu.  
♦461. SHRI RAMACHANDRA KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the Steel Authority of India is proposing to take over the Nilachal Ispat Nigam Ltd., 
Duburi. Orissa which was a joint venture of MMTC and the Government of Orissa; and 
(b)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STEEL (SHRI RAM VILAS PASWAN): (a) and (b) A Statement is laid on 
the Table of the House.  
Statement  
(a) The acquisition and tne merger of Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd. (NINE) with Steel Authority of 
India Ltd. (SAIL) was recommended by the Committee of Secretaries (CoS) in its meeting held on 
14.07.2005. Nilachal Ispat Nigam Limited located at Duburi. Orissa is a public limited company 
whose shares are jointly held by MMTC Limited, Industrial Promotion Investment Corporation of  

4    Oral Answers  [RAJYA SABHA]  to Questions  
Orissa Limited (IPICOL), Orissa Mining Corporation (OMC), National Mineral Development 
Corporation (NMDC) and other minority shareholders including banks and financial institutions.  
(b) As per the decision of the Committee of Secretaries (CoS) taken during its meeting on 14.07.2005, a 
Committee was constituted, under the Chairmanship o f Secretary, Department of Disinvestment 
with members from Ministry of Steel, Department of Commerce, Chief Secretary, Government of 
Orissa, Chairman, Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), Chairman-cum-Managing Director (CMD), 
MMTC Limited, Managing Director (MD), NINL and Joint Secretary (Steel) as the member-convener. 
The Committee had so far held four meeting on dates  21.02.2006. 06.03.2006, 09.08.2006 and 
05.09.2007. In accordance of the decision of this C ommittee taken during its third meeting on 
09.08.2006, a selection committee consisting of representatives from MMTC, SAIL and NINL finalized 
appointment of M/s IDBI Limited as merchant banker to valuate NINL's shares. The valuation report 
submitted by IDBI was discussed in the 4th meeting of the appointed Committee under the Chairmanship 
of Secretary (Disinvestment) on 05.09.2007, during which M/s IDBI also made a detailed presentation 
on the modalities adopted by it for valuation of NI NL shares. The weighted average value of NINL 
shares has been arrived at Rs. 27.62 by M/s IDBI. H owever, during the meeting on 05.09.2007 
Government of Orissa and MMTC both expressed  
their reservation on the valuation of NINL shares arrived at by M/s IDBI, which was later confirmed 
by them in writing.  
To resolve the issue further a meeting was convened by Commerce Secretary on 09.04.2008 attended 
by Secretary (Steel), Secretary (Steel & Mines), Government of Orissa, Chairman, SAIL and CMD. 
MMTC Limited. It has been decided that within seven days SAIL and MMTC Limited would suggest 
three names each for being appointed as independent  valuer to re-assess the value of NINL shares. 
Secretary (Steel) and Commerce Secretary would further decide on appointment of the mutually agreed 
investment banker to work out the valuation of NINL . On completion of these processes, a final 
decision in the matter would be taken by the Cabinet.  
SHRI RAMACHANDRA K.HUNTIA: Mr. Chairman. Sir. the Neelachal Ispat Nigam located at 
Duburi, Orissa, was started in the beginning of 1991-92. Subsequently, it had a joint venture with the 
State Government, MMTC. OMC and some other shareholders. Discussions for acquisition and merger 
of the Neelachal lspat Nigam Ltd. were held on 14.07.2005. TheTommittee under the Chairmanship 
of the Secretary, Disinvestments sat for four times, but could not take a concrete decision. Now the 
State Government is again arguing for the revaluati on of the factory after four years. The valuation 
was done by the IDBI...

SHRI RAMACHANDRA KHUNT1A: ...which is one of the reputed financial institutions. 1 would 
like to know whether there could be any other finnacial institution which is better than the IDBI. At 
present the value of the share of the Neelachal lspat Nigam Ltd. is Rs. 26/-. SAIL is prepared to give 
them the same value. The value of the share of SAIL  is Rs. 174. Even if there is a change in the 
valuation, it will have not effect. If SAIL is prep ared to give them the same value, why is the State 
Government not accepting it and the merger is not being done?

Need for review of Pulse Polio Programme  
*465. DR. K. KESHAVA RAO: Will the Minister of HEAL TH AND FAMILY WELFARE be 
pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that the Pulse Polio Programme needs a review in view of the cases reported 
in the first two months of the year 2008; 
(b)  if so, the details of the cases reported in States; and 
(c)  what concrete action Government is taking to fulfil its promise of total eradication of polio? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AMD FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBU MAN1 RAMDOSS): 
(a) to (c) A Statement is laid on th Table cf the House.  
Statement  
(a) and (b) National Polio Eradication Programme is  reviewed bi-annually by the India Expert 
Advisory Group on polio (IEAG) comprising of National and International Experts from World Health 
Organization (WHO), United Nation Children's Fund ( UNICEF) and Centre for Disease Control 
(CDC) Atlanta. The last review was undertaken on 19-20th December, 2007.  
The number of polio cases reported in the first two  months of the year are the tail end of 2007 
outbreak in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. The number of cases reported in the first two months are 163 out

of which 25 cases are from Uttar Pradesh and 134 cases from Bihar and 1 each from Orissa, Haryana, 
Maharashtra and Delhi.  
(c) The India Expert Advisory Group on Polio Eradication, which reviewed the programme in 
December, recommended that the programme continue to focus on Type 1 in view of its higher 
disease burden and propensity to cause large outbreaks and travel long distances to achieve polio 
eradication at the earliest, following steps have been taken by the Government in early part of 2008:— 
—  National Immunization days were implemented in January and February, 2008. mOPVI was 
used in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi and other high risk States and Districts and tOPV in other 
areas. 
—  Sub National Immunization Round was undertaken in March, 2008 in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, 
Delhi, Mumbai and other areas at risk using mOPV3 during 30th March, 2008. 
—  MoP Up immunization rounds have been implemented in response to detection of Wild polio 
virus in the State of Maharashtra, Haryana, Orissa. 
—  5 more Sub National Round is planned for implementation in UP, Bihar and other areas at 
risk during April, June, July, September and Octobe r, 2008. 
Union Health Minister convened meeting of the Health Ministers of polio affected States to discuss 
the issues and actions required by the State Governments for achieving the goal of zero polio 
transmission at the earliest in September, 2006 and June, 2007. The Health Ministers of the Sates 
assured that they are committed for eradication of polio from the country and necessary actions will be 
taken by the respective States to sustain good quality immunization rounds during the upcoming polio 
immunization compaings.  
The polio eradication strategy was reviewed by Union Health Minister with the experts of ICMR, 
UNICEF, WHO, NPSP, INCLEN and Rotary on 3rd April, 2008  
The Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar has been requested by Union Health Minister to 
monitor the programme at their level so that effective implementation of interventions takes place in 
their respective States.  
Secretary (Health & FW) reviewed the polio situation at regular intervals with the partners like 
WHO, UNICEF, Rotary and make appropriate decisions on the actions required for accelerating 
polio eradication activities.  
During the meeting with the State Health Secretaries in July 2007, Union Health Secretary apprised 
the State Health Secretaries regarding the polio situation and seek their support and commitment to 
achieve the goal of polio eradication.  
To ensure quality of immunization rounds and to achieve high coverage following actions are 
taken:—  
• Improved micro planning in all areas to ensure that no house is missed and no child 
left unvaccinated. Missed houses are revisited by teams. 
• Migratory populations from UP and Bihar are being i dentified in the States of 
Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and these migratory children are being cover during the 
SNID in UP and Bihar starting from August, 2007. 
• In the States of UP and Bihar every new born child is being identified and vaccinated 
during the polio immunization campaigns and is bein g tracked for 8 subsequent 
rounds. 
• In order to reach every eligible child during the pulse polio round, apart from the 
strategy of vaccinating children at fixed booths and house to house visits, efforts in 
vaccinating children in transit at railway stations, inside long distance trains, major 
bus stops, market places, religious congregations, major road crossings etc. through-
out the country have been itensified.

DR. K. KESHAVA RAO: Sir, I am satisfied with the answer of the hon. Minister, and I don't want 
to put any supplementary.  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Thank you. Any other supplementaries on this? ...(Interruptions)...  
SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: Sir, I have a supplementary on Q.No. 465.  
MR. CHAIRMAN: Yes; please, go ahead. ...(Interruptions)...  
SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT: Sir, it is a matter of concern that inspite all the efforts of the 
Government we have not succeeded in entirely eradicating polio. What I understand is that since polio 
is transmitted through the oral faecal and also through contamination of water, it is clear that just 
giving the oral polio vaccine may not really succeed in completely eradicating polio. We need a more 
comprehensive approach, Sir. Therefore, my question to the Minister is this. The Expert Committees 
which have been formed to monitor, that is fine, but at the same time, since other Ministers are also 
involved, for example, in sanitation, in clean water, etc. and all these are directly linked to the spread 
of polio, will the Minister consider having a Committee coordinating the various aspects so that a 
more comprehensive view on this campaign can be started?  
DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS: Sir, the hon. Member is right in saying that just giving polio 
drops will not suffice. On the other side, Sir, in the last few years, out of 35, we have been able to 
reduce the transmission of poliovirus in 33 States and Union Territories. Today we have come to a 
stage where there is endemicity of polio only in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. In the other States we have 
stopped the endemicity and transmission. Even though there may be some spordic cases due to Uttar 
Pradesh and Bihar because of migrants going out. So, those sorts of things are there. But coming back 
to the point, yes, Sir, the problem in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar is due to poor sanitation, poor 
environmental hygiene , high density of population and because of all these factors, inspite of our 
giving so much of polio drops, still the transmission goes on. But on the positive side, I would like to 
say that the National Rural Health Mission is perfectly envisaged for sanitation. It is a holistic component 
of health, sanitation, drinking water, nutrition, etc. So, the Ministry of HRD, the Ministry of Rural 
Development, the Panchyat Raj Ministry, the Women and Child Development Ministry and the Health 
and Family Welfare Ministry are working together in tandem. We have a Committee called the Mission 
Steering Group where all the Ministers are part of the Group and this Group decides holistically how 
at the grassroot level we can go about. The National Rural Health Mission is a very big boon to all the 
States including Uttar Pradesh and Bihar. I am very confident that in due course of time, we will 
definitely have a lot of facilities to provide clearn drinking water, nutrition, sanitation and also reduce 
the diseases, including polio. Sir, I have already said that there are only two States now, Uttar Pradesh 
and Bihar, and I have been personally talking to the Health Ministers and Chief Ministers. My Prime 
Minister has written letters to the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Among officers we had 
a lot of discussions. We had a series of meetings to discuss this problem. Now we have identified the 
high endemic blocks, rather than districts. The positive aspect is that there are two types of poliovirus 
one is the PI and the other is P3. We have eradicated P2 from India. PI is highly pathogenic and 
endemic and it transmits easily and it is very virulent but P3 virus is a little simpler and quieter virus. 
The good news is that this PI is not there in the whole of Uttar Pradesh. On the contrary, in Bihar we 
have problems in a few blocks. We are trying to address these problems. There are a number of missed 
children so we are going there. We are dedicating our entire staff focussing on these blocks.  

Oral Answers  [25 APRIL 2008]  to Questions   9  
SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Mr. Chairman, Sir, what I would like to know from the hon. Minister 
is this. He has already accepted in his answer that there is a major problem in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar 
to cope with the polio menace. What I am told is that, and I want to get it confirmed from the Minister, 
there are certain religious bodies and orthodox elements who have launched a propaganda that because 
of the polio vaccination the children would get impotent. That is a major impediment as far as polio 
vaccination programme is concerned. Is it true? If yes, what steps have been taken to combat this 
propaganda?  
DR. ANBUMANIRAMDOSS: Sir, it is true that we had problems in the past about some religious 
sects asking their children and mothers not to take  these polio drops. There were rumours that it 
would cause impotency and sterlity. All these types of rumours are spread and immediately we ask the 
State Governments to take cognizance of this issue. In participation with the State Governments and 
Rotary organisations, we have been going door-to-do or, village-to-village and block-to-block and 
discussing this with religious leaders. We have bee n using the advice and taking the help of the 
religious leaders of different religions and telling them that there is no problem around, and today we 
dont have much of this problem though there may be some sporadic cases.  
SHRI KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: We are thankful to the Gover nment that they are taking serious 
steps to eradicate polio in the country. Sir, there were some cases of deaths on oral polio in Assam.Due 
to these incidents, parents are hesitating to take their children to the polio booths in our State.The  
percentage of taking polio drops has become low. Si r, is the Government aware about the steps and 
what steps are taken by the Government?  
DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS: Usually, there are no deaths attributed to the dispensation of oral 
polio drops and if there are any, immediately we have the National Polio Surveillance Projects called 
the NPSP This is one of the largest surveillance projects in the entire world. NPSP has officers in all 
the States who would immediately go and notify if any case of death attributed to vaccine is there. We 
have not had any issues from Assam as well but sinc e the hon. Member has said, we will definitely 
look into that issue and take necessary action.

Non-payment of outstanding amount to sugarcane farmers  
†466. SHRI VEER PAL SINGH YADAV: 
SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:††  
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased 
to state:  
(a)  whether Government is aware that farmers of Uttar P radesh are not getting proper price of 
sugarcane; 
(b)  the reasons why farmers are not getting previous outstanding amount of sugarcane; 
(c)  whether the Central Government is taking any concrete measures in this regard; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and by when such measures would be taken; and 
(e)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC D ISTRIBUTION (SHRI 
SHARAD PAWAR): A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
Statement  
(a) The Central Government fixes the Statutory Mini mum Price (SMP) of sugarcane payable by 
sugar mills to the sugarcane growers for each sugar  season. The SMP is fixed on the basis of 
recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) and after consultations 
with the concerned stake holders and it is uniform for the whole country. However, some of the 
State Governments including the Government of U.P. have been fixing their own State Advised 
Price (SAP) of sugarcane which is generally higher than the SMP fixed by the Central Government. 
For 2007-08 sugar season, the Central Government fi xed the SMP of sugarcane at Rs. 81.18 per 
quintal linked to 9% recovery subject to premium of Rs. 0.90 per quintal for every 0.1% increase in 
the recovery above 9%. However, the Government of U .P. announced the SAP for 2007-08 sugar 
season as under:—  
(i)   Unapproved variety   -    Rs. 120 per quintal 
(ii)   General variety  -    Rs. 125 per quintal  
(iii)   Early variety  -    Rs. 130 per quintal  
The SAP so fixed by the Government of U.P. was chal lenged by some private sugar mills/ 
Private Sugar Mills Association in the Allahabad Hi gh Court. The Hon'ble Allahabad High Court 
(Lucknow Bench) vide its interim order dated 15th November, 2007 has dir ected payment of Rs. 
110 per quintal for all varieties of sugarcane for 2007-08 sugar season, subject to further order of 
the Court. Sugar mills are paying cane price as per the said interim order of the Hon'ble High Court.  
Similarly, though the SMP for the previous 2006-07 sugar season was Rs.80.25 per quintal 
linked to 9% recovery with premium as in the curren t sugar season for higher recoveries, the 
Government of U.P. had fixed the SAP at Rs.125 per quintal (general variety). The matter was 
litigated in the Allahabad High Court, which in its judgement dated 19th December, 2007, quashed

the order of the Government of U.P. fixing SAP for 2006-07 sugar season. However, the Hon'ble 
Supreme Court in its interim order dated 18th Janua ry, 2008 has stayed the said Allahabad High 
Court judgement and vide its interim order dated 27th February, 2008 has dir ected sugar mills to 
pay the cane price as under:  
(i)   Declined/unsuitable variety -    Rs. 115 per quintal  
(ii)   General variety  -    Rs. 118 per quintal  
(iii)   Early variety  -    Rs. 123 per quintal  
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has also ordered that if any payment has been made towards SAP, the 
same shall be adjusted from the amounts payable on the basis of the rates indicated above. If any 
payment has been made beyond the rate fixed above, there would not be for the present any refund.  
Thus, the matter relating to payment of cane price for 2006-07 and 2007-08 sugar seasons in U.P. 
is sub-judice.  
(b)  Due to high level of sugar production in the country during the last sugar season 2006-07 and 
the initial estimates of high sugar production during the current sugar season 2007-08, sugar prices in 
the county declined considerably which has constrained the capacity of the sugar mills to pay cane 
price to sugarcane growers in time. 
(c)  and (d) In order to help the sugar industry to clear the cane price arrears of sugarcane farmers, 
the Central Government has taken a slew of measures , the details of which are enclosed at 
Statement-! (See below). 
(e) Does not arise.  
Statement-l 
Details of steps taken by the Central Government to help the sugar industry 1 and sugarcane  
farmers  
(i) A butler stock of 20 lakh tons for one year created for the period 01.05.2007 to 30.04.2008.  
(ii) A buffer stock of 30 lakh tons created for the  period 01.08.2007 to 31.07.2008. The two 
buffer stocks involve annual subsidy of about Rs. 8 80 crore from the Sugar Development 
Fund (SDF) and additional bank credit of about Rs. 978 crore, and is aimed to enhance 
liquidity of sugar mills affected by decline in pri ces of sugar and stock value, for clearing 
cane price arrears as first priority.  
(iii) Export assistance to defray expenditure on tr ansport, marketing and handling charges and 
ocean freight @ Rs. 1.350/- per ton for sugar facto ries in coastal States and Rs. 1.450/- per 
ton for those in non-coastal'States subject to actuals by road/rail for export to the neighbouring 
countries, has been provided for one year from 19.0 4.2007 to 18.04.2008. The facility has 
been recently extended upto 30.09.2008 and is likely to involve maximum amount of Rs. 700 crore 
as assistance from SDF. and is aimed for clearing cane price arrears as first priority.  
(iv) The requirement of Release Orders for exports has been dispensed with from 3 1.07.2007.  
(v) The NABARD package of 2005 for restructuring of term loans of co-operative sugar factories 
has been expanded to include cooperative sugar fact ories not included earlier to avail the 
benefits, convert outstanding loans on account of harvesting and transport charges appearing 
in the factories' accounts as on 01.04.2007 upto maximum five years term loans without

interest subvention and enhancing budgetary support from Rs. 560 crore to Rs. 600 crore to 
provide maximum 3% per annum interest subsidy for r estructured term loans carrying an 
interest cap of 10% per annum.  
(vi) A loan scheme of about Rs. 3800 crore to exten d financial assistance to sugar undertakings 
has been formulated and implemented to provide additional liquidity support to the extent of 
notional excise duty on production of sugar in 2006-07 and 2007-08 sugar seasons exclusively 
earmarked for cane arrears/dues of 2006-07 and 2007-08 sugar seasons respectively relatable 
to SMP fixed by the Central Government. The total i nterest subvention estimated at about 
Rs. 1355 crore is to be borne from the Central Government budget (5% out of the maximum 
12% p.a. interest subvention and balance upto 7% p. a. from the SDF). As per information 
received from National Bank of Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD) and other 
scheduled commercial banks a sum of about Rs. 2482 erores has been sanctioned by them to 
concerned sugar factories. Further the proposals amounting to Rs. 464 erores are under process 
with the banks.  
(vii) To promote Ethanol Blending with Petrol (EBP), the following have been decided:  
(a)  5% ethanol blending made mandatory from October, 20 07 with 10% blending being 
made optional from October, 2007 and mandatory from October, 2008 except in Jammu 
& Kashmir, North-Eastern States and Island territories. 
(b)  Uniform Purchase Price of Rs. 21.50 per litre ex-factory for ethanol supplied by sugar 
factories for next three years. 
(c)  Permitting sugar factories to produce ethanol from sugarcane juice directly to give 
flexibility to sugar factories. 
(d)  Reduction in customs duty from 7.5% to 5% for denat ured alcohol and from 10% to 
5% on molasses when EBP programme at 5% level is fully operationalized.

Oral Answers  [25 APRIL 2008]  to Questions    15  
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: Up to 21 st April, 2008, the total cane price arrears of year 2006-07 was 
Rs. 1,015 crores and out of that, an amount has been paid in crores and actually the amount which has 
not been paid till 21 st is Rs. 324 crores. So, substantial amount has been already paid. The problem of 
Uttar Pradesh is altogether different from any othe r State. The Government of India on the 
recommendation of CACP had taken a final decision about the fixation of the price of cane and that 
price has been practically implemented by most of the States in the country. Uttar Pradesh Government 
has introduced their own price called the State Advisory Price. So, the State Advisory Price is always 
over and above whatever the price has been fixed for the whole country and this difference is because 
of that. This particular matter has gone to the court, the matter is before the court, matter is sub-judice 
and that is why whatever possible information we had to give, we have given here.

Buffer stock for emergency situations  
*469.    SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:  
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA:tt  
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased 
to state:  
(a)  whether Government has decided to form a strategic reserve of five million tonnes of foodgrains 
in addition to the buffer stock to meet emergency situations; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
tt The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shrimati Shobhana Bhartia.  

18   Oral Answers  [RAJYASABHA]  to Questions  
(c)  whether to maintain strategic reserves of foodgrains, adequate warehouses/godowns exist; 
(d)  if so, the capacity of such warehouses/godowns and whether new warehouses/godowns would 
be set up to maintain reserves of foodgrains; and 
(e)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC D ISTRIBUTION (SHRI 
SHARAD PAWAR): (a) to (e) A Statement is laid on the Table of the House.  
Statement  
(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. Pending revision of buffer norms and in order to ensure food security in the 
country, Government has decided that a strategic re serve of 50 lakh tonnes of foodgrains would be 
maintained by Food Corporation of India (FCI).  
The strategic reserve would be built up over a period of time starting from 2008-09.  
(c) to (e) The maxium buffer norm for foodgrains as on 1 st July is 269 lakh tonnes. As on 29.2.2008, 
the FCI has a total of 241.09 lakh tonnes of storage capacity. As on 29.2.2008, the Central Warehousing 
Corporation (CWC) and State Warehousing Corporation (SWC) have a storage capacity of 97.74 and 
186.28 lakh tonnes respectively. Therefore, capacity available with FCI, CWC, SWC and State agencies, 
is sufficient for storing the strategic reserve of foodgrains.

He says that the strategic reserve would be built up over a period of time starting from 2008-09. Could 
he tell the House by when this reserve would be built up? Is he talking about this fiscal year when we 
will have five million in surplus or is it an ongoing process?  
Secondly, Sir, he says that there is an adequate storage capacity. But, Sir, it is a known fact that, 
varying from 15 per cent to 30 per cent, our foodgrain is lost post-harvest because of the poor quality 
of storage. It is not a question of having the capacity, but it is a question of having the proper capacity. 
It should not go waste where in transportation or in gunny bags that store foodgrains, there are many 
leakages that cost us between 15-30 per cent. Does'nt the Government have any Official estimate as to 
how much is lost because of inadequate storage facilities, which are not up to the mark?  
SHRI SHARAD PAWAR: As far as the storage capacity is concerned, it is not a problem for the 
FCI. Whatever storage capacity is available with FCI, we are using that. Plus, we are using the Central 
Warehousing Corporation's storage capacity. We are also using the State Warehousing Corporation's 
storage capacity. By and large, whatever capacity is available in the country, out of that, we are using 
near about 50-55 per cent. Rest of the capacity is available even today.  
Regarding the question of its strategic reserve, it is not possible to implement that decision within 
one year. But our effort will be to build up the stock in the course of the next 2-3 years. This will be 
over and above the buffer stock and that will be ke pt as reserve. I think, we will be able to start, 
probably, building the stock from this year only. It may not be complete, but, at least, we will be able 
to start the process. One of the main reasons is that this year, we are getting a very good response from 
the farming community about our procurement. For instance, I am really happy to tell the House that 
till 24th April, that is, yesterday, the total wheat arrival in the market was 110 lakh tonnes. Out of that, 
we could procure 104 lakh tonnes, that is, 94 per cent. We have procured  36 lakh tonnes more as 
compared to last year, the same day. With regard to major States like Punjab and Haryana, this is the 
situation. Whatever is the daily arrival in Punjab,  out of that, we procured about 99.2 per cent and 
whatever is the daily arrival in Haryana, we procured 99.9 per cent. So, there is a tremendous cooperation 
and support from, particularly, these two States'. I am confident that the other States will also take  
inspiration from that. If this situation continues,  probably, we will be able to build up a strategic 
reserve from this year only.

*462.    SHRI DARA SINGH:  
SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:  
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government is aware that on account of non- payment, many hospitals in the capital 
are either refusing to be empanelled under Central Government Health Scheme or telling patients to 
pay upfront; 
(b)  whether it is a fact that CGHS owes Rs. 17,66,953 to AIIMS, Rs. 7 crore to Indraprastha Apollo 
Hospital, Rs. 3.5 crore to Max Healthcare, etc.; 
(c)  if so, what are the reasons therefor; and 
(d)  by when Government is expected to clear all such dues so that CGHS beneficiaries may not be 
put to any further hardships? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANIRAMADOSS): (a) 
to (d) No incident of refusal of treatment by priva te empanelled Hospital/diagnostic center for non-
payment of dues has been reported to the Government. As a matter of fact there are stringent provisions 
for penalties in cases of empanelled hospitals refuse to provide treatment.  
• During 2007-08, an amount of Rs. 115.75 crore has  been paid to private hospitals in Delhi.  
In respect of Indraprastha Apollo Hospital, bills amounting to Rs. 8.68 crore were pending as on 
1.4.2007 and during 2007-08, bills amounting to Rs. 73.00 lakhs were received. Payment of Rs. 7.38 
crore has been released during 2007-08 leaving unpaid bills of Rs. 2.03 crore as on 1.4.2008.  
In respect of Max Healthcare, Delhi, no bill was pending as on 1.4.2007 and during 2007-08, bills 
amounting to Rs. 3.80 crore were received. Payment of Rs. 2.34 crore has been released during 2007-
08, leaving unpaid bills of Rs. 1.46 crore as on 1.4.2008.  
Payment of bills of private empanelled hospitals & diagnostic centres is a continuous process and 
is subject to the availability of funds.  
In respect of AIIMS, the outstanding amount is to the extent of Rs. 17.50 lakh, as on 1.4.2008. Out 
of this amount, bills amounting to Rs. 15.00 lakh were returned by the Pay & Accounts Office as the 
bills were not counter-signed by the authorized signatory of AIIMS. After the bills are countersigned 
by the authorized signatory, the payment will be released by the Pay & Accounts Office, Ministry of 
Health & Family Welfare.  
Research contracts  
*463. SHRI KALRAJ. MISHRA: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be 
pleased to state:  
(a)  whether his Ministry awards research contracts to Consultants, NGOs, Academic and Research 
Organisations etc.; 
(b)  if so, trie list of research contracts with the name of the organizations which were awarded the 
research contracts in the last three years and their progress; 
(c)  whether the research contracts are displayed on the  website of his Ministry and if not, the 
reasons therefor; 

Written Answers to  [25 APRIL 2008]  Starred Questions   25  
(d)  the interna] process in deciding the topics of these research contracts; 
(e)  whether the research contracts were awarded through a competitive bidding process; and 
(0 if so, the criteria adopted therefor and if not, the sanctity of the award process?  
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS): (a) 
to (f) The Ministry of Health & Family Welfare carries out research activities through the Indian 
Council of Medical Research (ICMR), an autonomous organization under this Ministry.  
2. ICMR enters into collaborative arrangements wih other organizations including industry, 
International agencies, Government Departments and various public and private funded institutes in 
the areas of drug development, delivery techniques, diagnostics and devices, clinical trials etc. Funds 
on these researches are made available by these organizations and the technical expertise is given by 
ICMR.  
A:-Industry-ICMR Collaboration  
(i) The ICMR has a scheme undertaking research spon sored by Indian industry being 
implemented with the approval of Government of India.  
(ii) In the scheme, the industry approaches ICMR with a specific proposal for taking up 
R&D on payment.  
(iii) An agreement is entered into between the Industry and ICMR detailing the scope of 
work, budget, time-frame etc.  
(iv) The ICMR seeks legal advice on the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) 
submitted by the industry.  
(v) The funds are provided by the industry and the expertise is given by ICMR. Such 
projects are implemented after approval by the competent authority.  
(vi) The duration of the project could vary from 1- 5 years or more depending upon the 
project's aims and objectives.  
B:- International Agency-ICMR Collaboration  
(i) Collaborations between international agencies and ICMR, typically are initiated by 
Ministry of Health wherein R&D, clinical trial etc. for vaccines/drugs is envisaged 
as a need for India.  
(ii) All such projects are entered into with intern ational agencies like the WHO, only 
after approval of the Ministry of Health, Government of India.  
(iii) In such projects, the agreements are approved by the Ministry of Health and Family 
Welfare and implemented by the ICMR.  
3(a) Apart from the above, ICMR also funds Biomedical research in medical colleges, research 
institutes, hospitals, academic institutes, voluntary organizations etc. in the form of Extramural Research.  
3(b) Based on the National needs for disease control, ICMR initiates Task Force projects which 
are generally multicentric in nature. Experts from different institutes who are working in these areas 
are then invited to carry out research.  
3(c) Investigators from academic and research institutes apply for research grants to ICMR in form 
of Ad-hoc research schemes and fellowships. The projects are reviewed by respective Project Review 
Committees headed by the subject experts.

Delay in setting up of new AIIMS like institutions  
t*464. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN PANY: 
SHRI MAHMOOD A. MADANI:  
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  the details of the reasons for delay in setting up new institutions on the lines of All India 
Institute of Medical Sciences; 
(b)  the details of projects undertaken, so far, institution-wise; 
(c)  the details of funds allocated to each institution during the last five years, along with the 
amounts spent out of it; and 
(d)  the steps being taken by Government for early setting up of these institutions? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS): (a) 
to (d) The proposal for setting up of AIIMS-like in stitutions was approved by CCEA on 16.3.2006. 
The bid process for selection of the Project Consul tant for the entire project had been started in 
2004-05. This continued in 2006 but proved to be unresponsive. The offer of shortlisted Architectural 
Design Consultant for preparing enlarged concept de sign was rejected due to the exorbitantly high 
price quoted by the selected designer. Therefore, t he whole process had to be initiated de novo in 
December, 2006. Several methodological changes were made to ensure progress keeping in mind the 
complexity of building 6 such institutions simultan eously and lack of capacity for taking the whole 
project as one. Therefore, it was decided that each  AIIMS site would be taken as a separate and 
independent project instead of clubbing all six tog ether. The construction of housing complex was 
also separated from that of the Hospital and Medical College.  
The Design-DPR consultants have been selected for e ach site through open competitive bidding 
and lay-out master plans for each site have been ap proved. Preliminary architectural designs for the 
sites at Bhopal, Jodhpur and Rishikesh have been approved on 22.4.2008 and other three are likely to 
be approved in May, 2008. The detailed project reports (DPR) would be ready by July-August, 2008. 
Thereafter,.tenders would be invited for selection of contractor for civil construction work.  
In so far as construction of residential complex (housing & hostel) is concerned, bids were invited 
for selection of turn-key Developers. However, bid process was successful only for Jodhpur site . 
where work was awarded to M/s. Rajasthan State Road Development Corporation, aPSU of Government of 
Rajasthan and is in progress. The work relating to construction of residential complex at Rishikesh and 
Patna was entrusted to HLL and for Bhubaneswar and Raipur to HSCC. Concept plans for the 
residential complex at all the sites have been appr oved. Bids invited for selection of contractors for  
Bhubaneswar and Raipur sites by HSCC has turned uns uccessful due to exorbitant price quoted by 
bidders. It has been decided to re-tender for both the sites. Tenders for all the other 3 sites will b e 
issued in May, 2008.  
The work of residential complexes is likely to be completed by 2009-10 and the hospital-medical 
college complexes by 2010-11.

MDR-TB Patients in the Country  
*470. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased 
to state:  
(a)  whether it is a fact that daily 4400 TB patients die and number of MRD-TB patients is increasing 
in the country; 
(b)  if so, Government's response thereto; 
(c)  whether it is also a fact that around 20 per cent of TB patients, who are presently having TB, are 
actually availing re-treatment after having failed to comply with treatment regiments earlier, and 
(d)  if so, the details of steps taken or proposed to be  taken by Government to tackle this deadly 
disease? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS): (a) 
to (d) As per the latest estimates the number of de aths attributable to TB daily is ~900. Revised 
National TB Control Programme (RNTCP), by implementation of internationally recommended DOTS 
strategy and consistent efforts, has been able to bring down the number of deaths from —1400 per day 
in the pre-RNTCP days to the current level. WHO global report 2008 estimates a decline in the deaths 
due to TB from 42/lakh population per year in 1990 to 28/lakh population per year in 2006.  
Drug resistance surveillance studies undertaken in the past by premier institutes like Tuberculosis 
Research Centre (TRC), Chennai and National Tuberculosis Institute (NTI), Bangalore and the State  

Written Answers to  [25 APRIL 2008]  Starred Questions   29  
level studies undertaken in Gujarat and Maharashtra recently have shown that the prevalence of multi-
drug resistant TB has not increased over the past several years and is estimated to be -3% in new cases 
and 12-17% in re-treatment cases. The ongoing drug resistance surveillance undertaken by the TRC 
in its study area, from 1999 to 2004, has actually shown a decrease in the prevalence of MDR-TB.  
About 18% of all patients registered for treatment under RNTCP are re-treatment cases. However, 
large numbers of re-treatment cases are those who have taken non-standardized/inadequate/irregular 
treatment outside the programme in the past.  
The Revised National TB Control Programme (RNTCP), which is based on WHO recommended 
DOTS strategy, is being implemented in the entire c ountry. Under the programme, diagnosis and 
treatment facilities including the supply of anti TB drugs are provided free of cost to all TB patients. 
For quality diagnosis, more than 12000 microscopy centres have been established in the country.  
Treatment centres (DOT centres) have been established near to residence of patients to the extent 
possible. All government hospitals. Community Health Centres (CHC), Primary Health Centres (PHCs), 
Sub-centres asre DOT Centres, in addition, NGOs, Pr ivate Practitioners (PPs) involved under the 
RNTCP, Community Volunteers, Anganwadi workers. Women Self Groups etc. also function as DOT 
Providers/DOT Centres. Drugs are provided under direct observation and the patients are monitored 
so that they complete their treatment.  
To increase accessibility to the facilities provided under the Programme, special emphasis is laid 
on the 1EC activities, involvement of NGOs, private sector and medical colleges under the programme.  
The programme is in the process of establishing a n etwork of accredited Culture and Drug 
Susceptibility testing Intermediate Reference Laboratories (1RL) across the country, at least one in 
each state, in a phased manner for diagnosis and follow up of MDR TB patients. The IRL at Gujarat 
and Maharashtra have been accredited recently. Another 10 IRLs are under the accreditation process 
and are expected to be accredited in 2008. The remaining IRLs will be established and accredited by 
2009-10.  
The diagnosed MDR cases will be treated as per the DOTS Plus guidelines developed by the 
programme, in line with the international recommend ations. The treatment will be provided at the 
DOTS Plus sites at least one in each state, with qu alified staff to manage the patients, and have a 
system to deliver ambulatory DOT after an initial s hort period of in-patient care. The DOTS plus 
services have been rolled out in the states of Gujarat and Maharashtra in 2007. Remaining states will 
be covered under DOTS Plus by 2009-10.

Report of Quality Council of India on Pathological Laboratories  
*472. DR. K. MALAISAMY: 
SHRI S. ANBALAGAN:  
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  what is the core point in the report of Quality Cou ncil of India with special reference to 
pathological laboratories which are considered to be the backbone of medical profession; 
(b)  whether it is a fact that out of 25 lakh tests conducted every day, only one lakh are carried out 
in accredited laboratories and out of one lakh laboratories in India, only 100 are accredited by National 
Accredition Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories (NABL); 
(c)  the measures taken or being taken to set right this alarming situation; and 
(d)  the time-frame within which it can be done? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMAN1 RAMDOSS): (a) 
to (d) As per information received from Quality Council of India (QCI), they have not published any 
report on pathological laboratories in India.  
Accreditation of laboratories is done by the National Accreditation Board for Laboratories (NABL) 
which is an autonomous body, set up by QCI for the accreditation of testing and calibration of 
laboratories which include medical laboratories. Un der the process of Laboratories Accreditation, 
NABL gives formal recognition of technical competen ce for specific tests/measurements, based on 
third party assessment. Accreditation is a voluntary process wherein Laboratories apply for accreditation 
to the accreditation body for assessment against an International Standard, ISO 15189 in this case.  
NABL as on date has accredited 88 medical laborator ies with varying scope for each laboratory 
depending upon the competence of the laboratory and report from the expert assessors.  
For developing minimum standards for clinical establishments including diagnostic labs., the clinical 
establishments (Registration & Regulations) Bill, 2007, has already been introduced by this Ministry 
in Parliament. When enacted into a law, it will imp rove quality of health services by prescribing 
minimum standards for facilities & services with a view to standardizing health care services in the 
country.

t*474. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:

country; and

†476. SHRI JAI PARKASH AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD

In both the standards, tolerance limits for physical, chemical and toxic substances including pesticide

Shortage of manpower in healthcare sector  
*479. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HEA LTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether the country is facing an acute shortage of manpower in the healthcare sector and most 
of the physicians are migrating to developed countries like Britain and US; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether Government has formulated any strategy to meet the demand for doctors in the country's 
healthcare sector and to check the brain drain; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE (DR. ANBUMANI RAMDOSS): (a) 
to (d) As per information furnished by Medical Council of India (MCI), the total number of registered 
allopathic doctors in the country is 7,02,580. This , the allopathic doctor-population works out to 
1:1634. In addition, there are more than six lakhs practitioners of Indian Systems of Medicine and 
Homeopathy in the country. Taking all these numbers together, the doctor-population ratio comes to 
1:870. There are 271 medical colleges in the country with annual intake of 31,122 who add upto the 
existing medical manpower.  
In order to expand the facilities of the medical education and health related services, under Pradhan 
Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Yojna (PMSSY), the Governm ent has decided to set up six AIIMS like 
institutions in the under-served States and also to upgrade 13 existing Government medical colleges/ 
institutions in 10 States. Further, the Government encourages setting up of new medical colleges in 
the Government as well as private sector and also an increase in intake capacity of medical students. 
Under National Rural Health Mission (NRHM), all PHCs are envisaged to be strengthened by upgrading 
single doctor PHC to two-doctors PHC by posting of AYUSH practitioner and skilled nurses at PHG 
level.  
Government have also recognized the Post-Graduate Degrees given by institutions in five countries, 
viz. U.K., U.S.A., Canada, Australia and New Zeland, in order to remove barriers from and encourage 
the return of Indian doctors working overseas who may have acquired their specialist qualifications in 
these English speaking developed countries.

National Food Security Mission (NFSM) aims to enhance the production of Rice, Wheat and Pulses

Apprehension of virus capable to destroy wheat yields  
3409. SHRI D. RAJA:  
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI: 
KUMAR DEEPAK DAS: SHRI B.K. 
HARIPRASAD:  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government's attention has been drawn to a warning made by the United 
Nations (UN) that a rapidly sprading virus Ug-99 capable of destroying entire fields could 
wreak havoc in India; and 
(b)  if so, the details thereof and what preventive measures are being taken to protect our 
wheat fields against this virus attack, and at the same time increase wheat production? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE! MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE (SHRI KANTI 
LAL BHURIA): (a) Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) of the United Nations and 
warned wheat producing nations including India about the spread of Ug-99, an African race 
of black (stem) rust fungus of wheat.  
(b) According to experts, the effect, speed need the route of the movement of the fungus 
is unpredictable in near future. Therefore, at pres ent, it is only an apprehension that this 
African race may reach India.  
A vigil is kept on the movement of this race by Directorate of Wheat Research, Karnal, 
through international collaboration. Indian Council of Agricultural Research, in collaboration 
with the International Maize and Wheat Improvement Centre (CIMMYT), Mexico has taken 
steps to identify varieties possessing resistance against the new race of the stem rust fungus. 
A regular surveillance for pest and disease emergence in the country is conducted to take 
emergency measures, wherever required, through the Central Integrated Pest Management 
Centres, the Indian Council of Agricultural Research and the State Agricultural Universities 
and Departments.  
Also, the Plan quarantine regulatory system in the country prevents the introduction and 
spread of exotic pests and diseases that are destructive to crops by regulating/restricting the 
import of plant material and plan products. Post entry quarantine inspection is undertaken to 
ensure that imported plant material is free from any pests and diseases.  
A National Food Security Mission has been launched to increase the production inter-alia 
of wheat by 8 million tonnes by the end of the Eleventh Five Year Plan.

Essential drugs under price control  
3415. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS be pleased to to state:  
(a)  whether Government is considering to bring 354 essential drugs under price control; 
(b)  if so, the steps taken by Government in this regard; and 
(c)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CHEMICALS AND 
FERTILIZERS (SHRI B.K. HANDIQUE): (a) to (c) The Supreme Court vide its interim 
order dated 10-3-2003 in SLP (c) No. 3668/2003 directed the Government, inter-alia, to 
"consider and formulate appropriate criteria for ensuring essential and life saving drugs not 
to fall out of price control and further directed to review drugs which are essential and life 
saving in nature till 2nd May, 2003". As per the directions of the Supreme Court, the Ministry 
of Health and Family Welfare reviewed the National Essential Drugs List 1996 and brought 
out the National List of Essential Medicines 2003 (NLEM 2003).  
Keeping in view the directions of the Supreme Court it has been proposed in the draft 
National Pharmaceuticals Policy-2006 that basket of drugs for price control would be the 
formulations of specified strength of essential medicines as contained in the NLEM 2003 
(subject to certain exemptions) in addition to the 74 bulk drugs and formulations thereof 
which are at present under price control under the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 1995 and 
the formulations based thereon.  
This Policy was submitted before the Cabinet for its approval. The Cabinet considered 
the Policy in its meeting held on 11-1-2007. It was decided that the matter may, in the 
first instance, be considered by a Group of Ministers (GoM). GoM has since been 
constituted under the Chairmanship of Shri Sharad Pawar, Minister of Agriculture and 
Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, GoM has held three meetings 
so far on 10-4-2007,12-9-2007 and 30-1-2008. GoM is yet to make its recommendations 
to the Cabinet.

other drugs. There are no specific norms or guidelines to determine as to which drug can be 
classified as life saving drugs. Every drug in gene ral is considered useful in saving and 
prolonging of life.

3423. SHRI  S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:  
(a) the details of strategy evolved/planning drawn by Government for food security by 
e.g., strengthening buffer stock of wheat and rice, augmenting yields per acre etc., in view of 
the global forecast about shortage of food in the near future;  

66    Written Answers to  [RAJYA SABHA]  Unstarred Questions  
(b)  whether Government has been seized of the latest forecast about world rice production 
in 2008 made by Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) indicating an increase of estimated 
1.8 per cent in production; 
(c)  if so, whether Government has reviewed the prospect of the same in India vis-a-vis the 
ground realities; 
(d)  if so, the outcome thereof; and 
(e)  if not, the rationale therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH) : (a) The 
Government has been working on two major policy pla nks to ensure food security in the 
country. The first policy plank is to boost agricul tural production and productivity in the 
country by ensuring remunerative prices to farmers and supporting agricultural 
development programmes. The second policy plank bei ng followed is to insulate 
vulnerable sections of society especially Below Pov erty Line (BPL) and Antyodaya Anna 
Yojana families against shortfalls in availability of foodgrains and to keep market prices 
of foodgrains under check.  
Under these policies, the Government has taken a number of measures such as launching 
of National Food Security Mission and Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojna to increase production 
and productivity of cereals, pulses, oil seeds, fruits and vegetable crops during the 11 th Plan 
period. The Government has been implementing the Ta rgeted Public Distribution System 
(TPDS) and a number of welfare schemes under which allocations of foodgrains at highly 
subsidized prices are being made, particularly for BPL and Antyodaya Anna Yojana families 
and other vulnerable sections.  
The increased production and productivity of food and other crops are expected to help 
augment buffer stocks of wheat and rice in the Central Pool.  
(b) to (d) Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) of the UNO in its first forecast for 
the year 2008 has indicated an increase in the worl d production of rice by about 1.8%. As 
per FAO's publication No. 2, April, 2008 on crop prospects and food situation, India is not 
having shortfall in aggregate food production/supplies and forecast for total cereal production 
in 2008 is of 251.7 million tons.

SHRI HARISH RAWAT:

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH) : (a) Agencies like 
FAO, OECD and IGC during January-February, 2008 had  projected hardening of global 
food prices on account of lowest food inventories a round the globe. More specifically, 
however, in the list of 37 countries worldwide reported to be currently facing food crisis by 
UNFAO Report No. 2 (April 2008) — "Crop Prospects a nd Food Situation", India does not 
feature.  
(b)  UNFAO Report No. 2 (April 2008) — "Crop Prospects a nd Food Situation" has 
forecasted a rise of record 647 million tons (6.8% up from 2007), 441 million tons (1.8% up 
from 2007) of world wheat and rice production in 2008, respectively, and 1006 million tons 
of world food consumption of cereals (1% up from 20 07). 
(c)  and (d) Though India is not listed as one of the 37 countries facing food crisis as per 
FAO's Report No. 2 (April 2008), as also by International Grains Council — Grain Market 
Report (GMR 376 dated 28.3.2008), the Government in  all have initiated many remedial 
steps to keep Food Security of the country sacrosan ct, which broadly, inter alia, are (i) 
Fiscal Measures — reduction of tariffs to zero for rice, wheat, pulses, edible oils and maize, 
to 7.5% on hydrogenated oils and vegetable oils, to 30% on butter and ghee and withdrawing

MEP to regulate exports of onion and basmati rice, maintaining CIP for rice and wheat and

Amendment in essential commodities act to check price rise  
3428. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will the Minister of CON SUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether Government has expressed great concern over  price rise and its impact on 
'aam aadmi' and urged the State Governments to strengthen the PDS and act against hoarders 
and speculators; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the necessary amendments would be made in the Essential Commodities Act 
to give more powers to States to take action against hoarders and speculators; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (SHRI KANTILAL BHURIA): (a) and (b) Rise in prices 
as well as availability of Essential Commodities have remained the concern of the Central 
Government and accordingly State Governments/Union Territories are being advised from 
time-to-time to take appropriate action against hoarders under the provisions of "Essential 
Commodities Act, 1955" and "Prevention of Blackmarketing and Maintenance of Supplies 
of Essential Commodities Act, 1980". The Central Government has also been holding review 
meetings with Food Secretaries of all States/UTs with a view to ensuring smooth functioning 
of Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) in the country.  
(c) and (d) State Governments are vested with wide powers to take action against hoarders 
through State Control Orders issued by them under t he Essential Commodities Act, 1955. 
The Central Government has vide Notifications dated 29.8.2006 and 7.4.2008 further 
empowered State Governments by keeping in abeyance certain provisions of the Removal 
of (Licensing requirements, Stock limits and Movement Restrictions) on Specified Foodstuffs 
Order 2002. State Governments can now issue Control Orders regulating purchase, movement, 
sale, supply, distribution or storage for sale in respect of wheat, pulses, rice, edible oil and 
edible oilseeds. No further amendments to the Essen tial Commodities Act are under 
consideration.

AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:

(c)  whether Government is contemplating any scheme of Public Distribution System which 
would serve their poverty justifiably; and 
(d)  if so, the details of the scheme thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH) : (a) to (d) For 
allocation of foodgrains under TPDS, the accepted number of BPL families (including AAY), 
based on 1993-94 poverty estimates of Planning Comm ission and March 2000 population 
estimate of Registrar General of India, is 6.52 crores. However, the State & UT Governments 
have issued 10.28 crore BPL & AAY ration cards. Thus the BPL & AAY cards are more by 
3.76 crores. The Government got Targeted Public Distribution System (TPDS) evaluated by 
Programme Evaluation Organisation of Planning Commission and ORG MARG. Their reports 
received in 2005 pointed out high levels of exclusi on and inclusion errors in identification 
of eligible BPL families and diversion of foodgrains.  
In cases of exclusion errors, eligible BPL and Antyodaya families were not categorized 
as such. In cases of inclusion errors, ineligible families were found to have been categorized 
as BPL and Antyodaya households.  
To strengthen TPDS by eliminating exclusion and inc lusion errors in identification of 
eligible BPL and AAY families and by eliminating leakages and diversions of foodgrains, a 
nine-point Action Plan was evolved. This is under i mplementation by State and UT 
Governments. As part of this Action Plan and as stipulated under the PDS (Control) Order, 
2001, the State Governments have been directed to continuously review BPL and AAY lists 
so as to eliminate the APL families wrongly categorized as BPL and Antyodaya families and 
to include the genuine BPL and AAY families which m ight have been excluded while 
preparing the lists. This is a continuous process a nd is expected to result in inclusion of 
genuine poor in the lists of BPL and Antyodaya fami lies which might have been wrongly 
categorized as APL. This will result in proper targeting of the poor families so that they get 
the benefits meant for BPL and AAY categories.

Regulation of procurement of foodgrains 
3436. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN: Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government would regulate procurement of wheat and other cereals being
done by private traders in view of inflation rising to 5 per cent; 
(b) if so, what mechanism is in place to check hoarding by these traders;
(c) whether Government has also stopped export of rice and other grains to ensure food
security; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH): (a) and (b) As per 
the present policy the farmers have the option to sell their produce of wheat and other cereals 
to FCI/State Agencies at Minimum Support Price (MSP) or in the open market, as is 
advantageous to them. This ensures remunerative prices to the farmers. However, a notification 
titled "Wheat (Stock Declaration by Companies or Firms or Individuals) Order 2008" has 
been issued which provides that private parties who purchase wheat beyond 10,000 tonnes 
during 2008-09 shall furnish return to Secretary (Food), of the State from where maximum 
quantity has been purchased, while a return for purchase of wheat beyond 25,000 tonnes is 
required to be furnished to the Central Government. Similarly a notification titled "Rice 
(Stock Declaration by Companies or Firms or Individuals) Order 2007" has been issued 
which provides that any private party which purchases paddy (in terms of rice) or rice beyond 
10,000 tonnesduring Kharif Marketing Season 2007-08 shall furnish a return to the Secretary 
(Food), of the State from where maximum quantity has been purchased. In case the purchase 
of paddy (in terms of rice) or rice exceeds 25,000 tonnes (throughout the country) the return 
is to be filed with the Central Government. Funher Department of Consumer Affairs has 
issued orders enabling State Governments to impose stock limit on wheat, rice pulses, edible 
oils and edible oilseeds to check hoarding. 
(c) and (d) Export of non-basmati rice on private account has been banned. Export of
wheat on private account has already been banned by the Government till further orders. 
Export of rice, wheat and wheat products from the Central Pool is also banned till further 
orders.

Hoarding of food grains by traders 
3437. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA: 
SHRI D. RAJA: 
Will the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the rampant hoarding of foodgrains by traders had been the main reason for
the low procurement by FCI during the year 2007-08 and shortage of foodgrains in the 
market and resultants price rise; 
(b) if so, whether the Essential Commodities Act has been implemented in the States
properly; 
(c) if not, what action has been taken for its proper implementation;
(d) whether Government has any proposal to give more teeth to the Act to prevent hoarding
by traders; and 
(e) if so, the details thereof?
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD 
AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION (DR. AKHILESH PRASAD SINGH): (a) to (c) The 
Procurement of foodgrains by FCI during 2007-08 has been higher than 2006-07. Procurement 
of wheat increased to 111.28 lakh tonnes in Rabi Marketing Season (RMS) 2007-08 as 
compared to 92.26 lakh tonnes in RMS 2006-07. Procurement of rice in Kharif Marketing 
Season (KMS) 2007-08 has been 218.4 lakh tonnes (uptil 31.03.08) as compared to 206.31 
lakh tonnes in the corresponding period of KMS 2006-07.  
In order to check hoarding of foodgrains and resultant price rise, the State Governments 
have been delegated powers under Essential Commodities Act, 1955 to impose suitable 
stock limits on certain essential commodities. To have an assessment of major purchases of 
foodgrains by private trade and check evasion of taxes, Orders were issued by the Central 
Government making it mandatory for any company/firm/individual to declare purchases 
beyond 50,000 tonnes of wheat during RMS 2007-08 and 10,000 tonnes of rice during KMS 
2007-08. 
The enforcement of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 lies with the State Governments/ 
Union Territories who have been delegated powers to take necessary action under the 
provisions of said Act. The Central Government is regularly monitoring the action taken by 
States/UTs through monthly report from them. The States/UTs have also been advised to 
strengthen their enforcement machinery to prevent malpractices in essential commodities 
and take necessary action against the unscrupulous persons indulging in hoarding and black 
marketing of essential commodities. 
(d) and (e) Central Government vide its Notification dated 29.08.2006 have empowered
States/Union Territories to fix stock limits in respect of wheat and pulses so as to enable 
them to take appropriate actions against the hoardings of these two commodities. The validity 
of this order has been extended upto 31.08.2008. Similarly for edible oils, edible oilseeds 
and rice States/Union Territories have been empowered to fix stock limits for one year and 
take necessary action against hoardings and speculation.

3451. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND 
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether a number of polio cases have been reported in the country during 2007 and so

Written Answers to  [25 APRIL 2008]  Unstarred Questions   93  
(c)  whether the reasons for this state of affairs have been evaluated and if so, the details 
thereof; and 
(d)  the steps taken/proposed to be taken to tackle the problem? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND  FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) Yes Sir. Number of Type 3 Polio 
case reported in 2007 and so far in 2008 is high in comparison to Type 3 polio cases reported 
in 2006. But number of Type 1 polio cases reported during same period is quite low in UP 
and Bihar.  
(b)  The number of Polio cases reported during 2007 and so far in 2008 is given in the 
Statement (See below). 
(c)  Yes Sir. National Polio Eradication Progamme was re viewed by the India Expert 
Advisory Group on polio (IEAG) comprising of Nation al and International Experts from 
World Health Organization (WHO), United Nation Children's Fund (UNICEF) and Centre 
for Disease Control (CDC) Atlanta on 19-20th December, 2007. The observations of IEAG 
are as under: 
 
* Due to accelerated immunization rounds and use of monovalent oral polio vaccine 
1 (mOPVl) in 2007, wild polio virus type 1 (WPV1) transmission is at low level. 
* The population immunity against WPV1 among children in India is high. 
* The 'core' districts of western Uttar Pradesh (in M oradabad, Meerut, 
Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh and Bareilly sub-divisions) have not reported WPV1 since 
November, 2006. 
The IEAG Recommended that in the first half on 2008 the activities should be undertaken 
with the objective of interrupting WPV1 transmission in the low transmission season, while 
maintaining good control of wild polio virus type 3 (WPV3).  
(d) Following steps have been taken by the Government to tackle the problem:—  
—  National Immunization days were implemented in January and February, 2008, 
mOPVl was used in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi and o ther high risk States and 
Districts and tOPV in other areas. 
—  Sub National Immunization Round was undertaken in M arch, 2008 in Uttar 
Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi, Mumbai and other areas at ri sk using mOPV3 on 30th 
March, 2008. 
—  MoP Up immunization rounds have been implemented in  response to detection 
of Wild polio virus in the state of Maharashtra, Haryana, Orissa. 
—  5 more Sub National Round is planned for implementation in UP, Bihar and other 
areas at risk during April, June, July, September and October, 2008. 
To ensure quality of immunization rounds and to achieve high coverage following action 
are taken:—  
* Migratory populations from UP and Bihar are being i dentified in the States of 
Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and these migratory children are being covered during 
the SNID in UP and Bihar starting from August, 2007 . 
* In the States of UP and Bihar every new born child is being identified and 
vaccinated during the polio immunization campaigns and" is being tracked for 8 
subsequent rounds.

Plan to address the menace of deafness  
3461. SHRIMATI KANIMOZHI: Will the Minister of HEAL TH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  the average number of children born deaf every year and the percentage of population 
in the country suffering from progressive and acute hearing loss; 
(b)  whether Government has any plan to address the menace of deafness; 
(c)  if so, the details thereof; and     
(d)  whether it is also proposed to start ENT Departments in every district hospital in the 
country and to provide adequate care to the hearing impaired? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND  FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) NSSO 58th round (2002) reveals 
that the Prevalence rates of hearing impaired among the children below 4 years was 55 both 
in rural and urban areas.  
It has identified hearing impairment in terms of pr ofound, severe and moderate cases. 
The data depicts that among the hearing impaired persons 31.1% cases had profound, while 
39.8% cases had severe and the rest 29% cases had m oderate hearing impairment in the 
rural areas. In the case of urban areas 34.5% had profound, 36.2% had severe while the rest 
29.3% have moderate hearing impairment.  
(b) and (c) To address this huge burden of Hearing impairment, the pilot phase of National 
Programme and Prevention and Control of Deafness (NPPCD) has been launced in 25 districts 
of 10 States and one U.T. in 2007.  
This programme is being extended to 203 districts d uring the Eleventh Five Year Plan 
(2008—2012).  
(d) Under the programme (NPPCD), Capacity Building of the entire identified District 
hospitals will be undertaken in the programme by pr oviding ENT and Audiology 
Equipments along with One Audiometric Assistant and  One Special Educator (Instructor 
for the Young Hearing Impaired) to the district Hos pital to provide adequate care to the 
hearing impaired.

surgeon in each district hospital.

Revamping the Existing Polio Eradication Strategy  
3469. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of HE ALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a) whether, with generous assistance and involveme nt of WHO and UNICEF in the 
National Polio Eradication Programme, India still has the highest number of Polio cases in 
the world;  

Written Answers to  [25 APRIL 2008]  Unstarred Questions    109  
(b)  whether Government has examined the Global Polio Eradication Initiative data released 
recently clubbing India with Pakistan, Nigeria and Afganistan where Polio is still an epidemic; 
(c)  whether based upon these data, Government proposes to revamp the existing polio 
eradication strategy; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND  FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) Yes Sir. India has highest number 
of polio cases in the world this year. However, impressive progress has been made in curtailing 
transmission of Wild Polio Virus Type 1 in the country. Most polio cases in 2008 are of type 
3 polio virus. The type 3 incidence is declining ra pidly following immunization rounds in 
Uttar Pradesh and Bihar with monovalent oral polio vaccine type 3 (mOPV3).  
(b) Yes Sir. 
(c)  and (d) The India Expert Advisory Group on polio (I EAG) comprising of National 
and International Experts from World Health Organization (WHO), United Nation Children's 
Fund (UNICEF) and Centre for Disease Control (CDC) Atlanta reviewed the Pulse polio 
Programme on 19-20th December, 2007. The IEAG suggested that in the first half of 2008 
the activities should be undertaken with the objective of interrupting WPV1 transmission in 
the low transmission season, while maintaining good  control of wild polio virus type 3 
(WPV3). 
Following steps are taken by the Government to achieve goal of zero transmission:—  
—  National Immunization days were implemented in Janu ary and February, 2008. 
mOPVl was used in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Delhi and other high risk States and Districts 
and tOPV in other areas. 
—  Sub National Immunization Round was undertaken in March 2008 in Uttar Pradesh, 
Bihar Delhi, Mumbai and other areas at risk using mOPV3 on 30th March, 2008. 
—  MoP Up immunization rounds have been implemented in  response to detection of 
Wild polio virus in the State of Maharashtra, Haryana, Orissa. 
—  5 more Sub National Round is planned for implementation in UP, Bihar and other 
areas at risk during April, June, July, September and October, 2008. 
To ensure quality of immunization rounds and to achieve high coverage following actions 
are taken;—  
• Migrat6ry populations from UP and Bihar are being identified in the States of Punjab, 
Haryana, Gujarat and these migratory children are being covered during the SNID in 
UP and Bihar starting from August, 2007. 
• In the States of UP and Bihar every new born child is being identified and vaccinated 
during the polio immunization campaigns and is bein g tracked for 8 subsequent 
rounds. 
• In order to reach every eligible child during the p ulse polio round, apart from the 
strategry of vaccinating children at fixed booths and house to house visits, efforts in 
vaccinating children in transit at railway stations, inside long distance trains, major 
bus stops, market places, religious congregations, major road crossings etc. through 
out the country have been intensified.

Welfare is reviewing the situation on continuous ba sis. All the major hospitals are fully

t3491. SHRI RUDRANARAYAN PANY: Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY 
WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether it is mandatory to put the logo of danger a longwith health warning on the 
packings of tobacco products; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether some of the tobacco products have been give n exemption from this legal 
requirement; 
(d)  if so, the details thereof; and 
(e)  the steps taken by Government to bring all tobacco products under this regulation? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND  FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) to (e) Section 8 of the "The Cigarette 
and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertis ement and Regulation of Trade and 
Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003" provides for display of specified

Suicides in the Country  
3494. SHRIMATI SUPRIYASULE:  
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR SANGHI:  
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a)  whether teen suicides in the country are among the highest in the world and suicides 
are the major problem worldwide with the highest rate being among the elderly in the west 
and among teens in the country bringing greater socio-economic loss due to the death of the 
young population in the country; 
(b)  whether according to doctors, reports, suicides among young women are the highest 
in two countries, India and China; 
(c)  whether suicides are very high in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry; 
(d)  the main reasons of such highest teen suicides in the country; and 
(e)  the concrete measures Government proposes to take to check this? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH AND  FAMILY 
WELFARE (SHRIMATI PANABAKA LAKSHMI): (a) and (b) According to National Crime 
Records Bureau (NCRB), no data on incidence of suic ide in other countries is available. 
However, in the country, a total of 2913, 2555 and 2464 victims of suicide during 2004 to 
2006 were in the age group 0 to 14 years and a total of 40136, 40234 and 42216 victims of 
suicide in the same period belonged to the age group 15 to 29 years. A total of 9213, 9317 
and 9127 victims of suicide during 2004 to 2006 wer e aged 60 years and above. Loss of 
young people due to suicides leads to major socio-e conomic losses as it spans through 
productive age-group of the country. According to N CRB, a total of 41046, 40998 and 
42410 suicides by females were reported in the country during 2004 to 2006.  
(c) According to National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB), the rates of suicide in Kerala, 
Tamil Nadu and Puducherry are very high during the years 2004 to 2006.  
(d)  Suicic-es occur due to a combination of physiologic al, social, cultural, economic, 
interpersonal and medical reasons. Causes are most of the times interlinked, cumulative and 
progressive in nature! 
(e)  It is envisaged to restrategise" the National Menta l Health Programme during the 
Eleventh Five Year Plan period to include suicide prevention, stress management, counseling 
services for Schools and Colleges under District Mental Health Programme with active

Will the Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERP RISES be pleased to 
state:  
(a)  what is the status of export of coir products in India; 
(b)  what are the details of incentives that are proposed to be given to the industry to boost 
exports of these products; 
(c)  whether Government is aware that Orissa has good potential in coir sector; and 
(d)  if so, what is the action plan of the Centre to hel p the State to exploit this sector to 
improve its rural economy? 
THE MINISTER OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES  (SHRI 
MAHAVIR PRASAD): (a) The export of coir products to the tune of 1,86,481 MT valued 
at Rs. 588.79 crore (Provisional) were realized in 2007-08 as compared to the export of 
168754 MT coir products valued at Rs. 605.17 crore during 2006-07.  
(b) The incentives proposed for boosting up export of coir products are briefed below:—  
(i) Duty credit scrip of 1.5% under the Duty Entitlement Pass Book Scheme of Ministry 
of Commerce.  
(ii) Cash incentive ranging from 1% to 12.5% as per  classification as per the Duty 
Drawback scheme of Department of Revenue.  
(iii) Duty free scrip of 1.25% for selected product s under the Focus Product Scheme of 
Ministry of Commerce.  
(iv) Duty credit scrip of 2.5% for all coir product s under the Focus Product Scheme of 
Ministry of Commerce.  
(v) Subvention by lowering the interest rates of pre-shipment and post shipment credits 
by 2.5%.  
(vi) Assistance under various Foreign Trade Policy Schemes like Export Promotion Capital 
Goods (EPCG) scheme, Advance Authorization Scheme, etc.  
(vii) Incentives under External Market Development Assistance Scheme of the Coir Board 
for undertaking various export promotion activities viz. Participation in Fairs/Buyer 
Seller Meets/Trade Delegations, etc.  
(viii) Financial assistance under Market Access Initiative Scheme and Market Development 
Assistance Scheme of Ministry of Commerce for specific export activities.

products.

t3496. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN: Will the Minister of MI CRO, SMALL AND 
MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to state:  
(a)  the details of the various schemes implemented by G overnment for revival of the 
small scale industries; 
(b)  the number of the small scale industries who as a result of implementation of abovesaid 
schemes received revival packages, State-wise, Union Territory-wise and industry-wise; and
