the country, State-wise and Union Territory-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES  (SHRI 
MAHAVIR PRASAD): (a) and (b) The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises 
does not provide any direct financial assistance fo r rehabilitation of sick micro and small 
enterprises (MSEs). However, financial assistance, by way of debt restructuring, including 
fresh loans, for the rehabilitation of sick MSE is provided by the primary lending institutions 
(PLI), including commercial banks, which provide credit to the MSEs. For this purpose, the 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has issued detailed gui delines to banks in January, 2002 on 
detection of sickness in MSE at an early stage and taking remedial measures and for 
rehabilitation of sick MSEs identified as potentially viable. Further, RBI has issued guidelines 
on 8th September, 2005, based on the "Policy Package for Stepping up Credit to Small and 
Medium Enterprises (SMEs)" announced by the Central Government on 10th August, 2005. 
These guidelines relate, inter alia, to viability criteria, prudential norms for restruc tured 
accounts, provision of additional finance and time-frame for working out the restructuring 
package and its implementation.  
As per the data compiled by the RBI from the schedu led commercial banks, 588 viable 
sick MSEs were put under nursing at the end of Marc h, 2007. The State/Union Territory-
wise position is given in the Statement {See below). The industry-wise information on sick 
MSEs put under nursing is not compiled by the RBI.

following statement regarding the State of Jammu and Kashmir.  
"As the Hon'ble Members are aware, a process of wide-ranging consultations with different 
sections of the people in the State of Jammu and Ka shmir regarding various aspects of the 
situation in the State had been initiated in the form of the Round Table Conference (RTC) on 
Jammu and Kashmir under the Chairmanship of the Hon 'ble Prime Minister in February, 
2006. In pursuance to the 2nd RTC held at Srinagar on 24-25 May, 2006, five Working 
Groups were constituted to look into various aspects and recommend measures for bringing 
about further improvement in terms of restoration of peace and normalcy and for the overall 
balanced and socio-economic development of the people in the State. The reports of four of 
these Working Groups were presented in the 3rd RTC held in New Delhi on 24 April, 2007, 
which broadly endorsed the approach and recommendations made by them.  
The Working Group on 'Confidence Building Measures across the segments of Society in 
the State' had made various recommendations, inter-alia, in respect of relief and rehabilitation 
measures for widows, orphans and other victims of m ilitancy and violence, facilitating the 
return and rehabilitation of the Kashmiri migrants, issues relating to refugees of 1947 from 
West Pakistan in POK, etc. After examination of the recommendations, the Government has 
taken the following decisions:  
Victims of Militancy Related Violence  
In 1994, the State Government of Jammu and Kashmir evolved a special scheme for 
providing compassionate employment to the eligible next of kin (NoK) of victims of militancy 
related violence. Due to non-availability of adequate number of jobs, there is a large backlog 
of approved cases for such compassionate appointment. There are also a number of families 
where, despite relaxations in eligibility conditions, there are no members in the family eligible 
for employment. It was proposed by the State Govern ment, as an exceptional measure, to 
offer a one-time compensation of Rs. 5 lakhs in lieu of the agreed compassionate appointment. 
They have sought the assistance of the Government o f India for re-imbursement of the 
expenditure that coverage of the backlog will entai l. We have agreed to the request of the 
State Government.  
We have also agreed to the request of the State Gov ernment to provide assistance for 
their proposal to increase the quantum of monthly p ension payable to widows under the 
existing scheme of the Rehabilitation Council of J & K to Rs. 750/- per month from the 
present level of Rs. 500/- per month. Assistance to those orphaned in militancy related violence 
will now cover all such children without discrimination.  
Problems of Migrants of the Valley  
A major issue that has plagued the situation in Jammu and Kashmir is the fact that more 
than 55000 families who had been forced to leave their homes in the wake of the unfortunate 
events in the State, continue to be away from their homes in the Kashmir Valley. There is a 
longstanding tradition in the State of Jammu and Kashmir of people of different faiths living 
together in peace and harmony. We have a collective responsibility to rectify the situation,  
  

Statements by  [25 APRIL 2008]  Minister    179  
and to facilitate the return of these families, who are an integral part of the composite social 
fabric of the area and, in the process, address a m ajor humanitarian concern that has been 
crying for attention over the years.  
When they left the Valley, many migrant families ha d to resort to distress sale of their 
houses and properties in the Valley till legislatio n put a stop to it in 1997. The State 
Government is being requested to identify land for group housing societies of such families. 
The Government proposes to give these migrants families, who opt to return to the Valley, a 
lump sum grant of Rs. 7.5 lakh to build or buy homes through such societies.  
It has also been decided to give a similar lump sum  grant to migrant families whose 
houses have been fully or partially damaged, as wel l as assistance to those whose houses 
may not have been damaged, but may have got into di suse and dilapidation as a result of 
abandonment. It is proposed to assist suitably with transit accommodation and start-up  
expenses.  
It has also been decided that the monthly relief be ing presently given to around 15,000 
migrant families in Jammu and Delhi will be continued for such of thesse families, who may 
opt to return to the Valley, for a period of two years to enable a smooth transition.  
The Government will also provide assistance for education of children of migrant families 
through the J&K Rehabilitation Council.  
The State Government has proposed to provide 6000 jobs, for the educated among migrant 
youth, in the State Government service. To assist t he State Government in providing such 
employment opportunities, the Central Government wi ll bear the cost towards salary for 
about 3000 youth till they are absorbed against regular posts in the State Government, within 
the specified time-frame. Further, the Government i s considering a financial package for 
other unemployed youth from among the migrant community to help them engage in self-
employment through vocational training.  
The migrant families who are engaged in agriculture  and horticulture would require 
assistance to renew their occupation in the field. We will provide lumpsum grants for 
restoration of agricultural holdings and orchards which may have been lying abandoned.  
We are examining the feasibility of waiving the interest on unpaid loans taken by Kashmiri 
migrants before their migration as part of a one-time settlement package.  
The expenditure on all the above proposals is presently estimated to be around Rs. 1600 
crore. These benefits will apply to all migrant families, who migrated bag and baggage after 
1989, and have not been able to return to the valley. We hope that these measures will go a 
long way in bringing these families back home, and enable them to get back to a life of 
dignity and honour in the land of their forefathers where they belong.  
Refugees from West Pakistan  
We are conscious of the hardship that the refugees from West Pakistan have had to face 
because they are not considered to be permanent residents of the State. We have decided to 
work out a package for them.  
Firstly, a dispensation is proposed to enable their  children and grand children to seek 
admission in technical educational institutions in various parts of the country. Secondly, it is 
proposed to facilitate bank loans without security of land. A nodal cell will be~set up by the

Union Ministry of Finance to deal with this matter.  Thirdly, we will provide vocational 
training opportunities under the Skill Development Initiative Programme of the Government 
of India.  
PoK Refugees of 1947  
We have also examined the problems faced by the families who migrated from PoK to the 
State of J&K in 1947. On the recommendations of the State Government, we have agreed to 
meet an expenditure of about Rs. 50 crores to resolve cases of land deficiency or where it 
has not been possible to allot plots in urban areas to these families. With these measures no 
further assistance will be required from the Government of India. We expect that this will 
bring the problem of PoK refugees of 1947 to rest.  
Problems of compensation for lands used for construction of Border Works  
In respect of a large quantum of the lands on which various border works, such as ditch-
cum-bunds, border fencing, etc., were constructed, compensation remains to be paid to the 
affected farmers. Time bound steps will be taken fo r payment of compensation as per the 
law.  
We had also given directions that, wherever public premises related to essential public 
services like education, health, water supply, etc. , are being used by the security forces 
deployed in the State, measures may be taken to relocate, and in the case of private property 
being so used, payment of adequate rent may be ensured. I am happy to inform the House 
that over the past year significant progress has been achieved in this regard.  
With a view to further consolidate the confidence building initiatives already taken, it is 
planned to liberalise the entry permit system of cross LoC travel, by bringing in features like 
triple entry permits valid for one year and completion of the verification process within six 
weeks. We are also proposing early operationalisation of Kargil-Skardu and Jammu-Sialkot 
routes, and increasing the frequency of Srinagar-Muzaffarabad and Poonch-Rawalakot bus 
services to weekly from the present fortnightly. We  will discuss these issues shortly with 
Pakistan. For convenience of travellers, applications for entry permit can be made at each 
District Passport Collection Centre. These measures will expand travel across the LoC and 
also enable wider cultural, academic, students and other exchanges. Trade and truck services 
across the LoC will also be operationlised."
